/**
 * CSV files the practice opens in Excel. A value that starts with = + - @ (or a
 * tab or carriage return) is kept as text with a leading apostrophe, so a
 * client's name or note can never run as a formula when the file is opened.
 * Plain numbers, negative ones included, stay numbers.
 */
export function csvCell(value: unknown): string {
  if (value === null || value === undefined) return ''
  let s = String(value)
  if (/^[=+\-@\t\r]/.test(s) && !/^[-+]?\d+(\.\d+)?$/.test(s)) s = `'${s}`
  return /[",\n\r]/.test(s) ? `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"` : s
}

export const csvText = (header: readonly string[], rows: ReadonlyArray<readonly unknown[]>): string =>
  [header.map(csvCell).join(','), ...rows.map((r) => r.map(csvCell).join(','))].join('\r\n')
